name: Interpretable Machine Learning (3rd ed.)
what: Christoph Molnar's open reference for model-agnostic XAI: LIME, SHAP/SHAPley, permutation/LOFO importance, ALE, partial dependence, plus DNN-specific methods. For IntelliCell it is the single source to justify/validate the SHAP-for-NTI step (additive index) and to explain the 4 extracted morphological features; the DNN chapters cover segmentation/heat-map saliency context.
why_better: The old plan lists 'SHAP-only XAI' with no grounding text; a dedicated, critically-reviewed book that discusses strengths/weaknesses of each method -> prevents misusing SHAP and lets the team pick the right attribution method per output (segmentation map vs scalar NTI).
evidence: n/a (educational book); 3rd edition adds LOFO + Ceteris Paribus chapters. Free online, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
source_title: Interpretable Machine Learning: A Guide for Making Black Box Models Explainable

why_better: Old plan jumps to SHAP with no framework for explaining/validating the index; EMA gives a principled explain+examine workflow for the additive NTI -> more defensible thesis XAI section than ad-hoc SHAP.
evidence: n/a (open textbook); online at ema.drwhy.ai, companion repo pbiecek/ema.

name: A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction and Distribution-Free UQ
what: Angelopoulos & Bates' self-contained free document (with Python code + Jupyter notebooks) on conformal prediction. For IntelliCell it is the learning source to attach statistically valid, distribution-free confidence intervals to the scalar NTI and to per-parameter (length, branch count, soma) estimates, plus coverage under distribution shift (across doses/time).
why_better: Old plan's UQ is temperature scaling + ECE (calibration only, no guaranteed intervals); conformal prediction gives finite-sample coverage guarantees -> a genuinely new, rigorous uncertainty deliverable the old plan lacks, with minimal extra compute.
evidence: n/a (tutorial); extends to structured outputs, distribution shift, abstention. 409-MRI ordinal-conformal companion (arXiv:2207.02238) shows tight coverage in medical imaging.
source_title: A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction and Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification
license: free (arXiv) + open code; permissive (unverified exact license)

name: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions (SHAP)
what: Lundberg & Lee (2017) - the landmark paper introducing SHAP: unifies six existing additive-attribution methods and proves uniqueness of the Shapley-value solution. It is the learning source the team must cite for the NTI additive index: it is exactly why SHAP is the right additive decomposition of a toxicity score into per-feature contributions.
why_better: Old plan uses 'SHAP-only' without citing its foundation; this is the canonical, citable source for additive explanations of the NTI -> the single most important XAI citation for the additive-index claim.
evidence: Unifies six methods; introduces KernelSHAP/TreeSHAP/DeepSHAP; widely reproduced (no single benchmark - it is the method/proof paper).
